mechanism_narrative: Sustained improvement in TRANSIT mobility from -34.4 to -29.1 over four weeks signals restored commuting and errand trips, which mechanically lifts RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT continues to rise over the next 28 days while RETAIL_REC mean is lower than its last 28-day mean, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the weekly mean WORKPLACES mobility crosses above -20 (less negative), workplace re-entry crosses a critical threshold that increases weekday retail footfall, so RETAIL_REC rises over the following two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES t-0w = -19.1, first crossing above -20 in the four-week window
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES is above -20 for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not exceed its last 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility (fewer people staying home) combined with a rise in TRANSIT mobility signals substitution from home confinement to out-of-home activity, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 11.1 to 9.4 while TRANSIT rose from -34.4 to -29.1
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL falls and TRANSIT rises over the next 28 days but RETAIL_REC mean is lower than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Under renewed restriction regime, a rise in GROCERY_PHARM toward baseline together with elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility indicates a return to home-centered consumption and mobility restrictions, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -2 and RESIDENTIAL rises above 10
failure_condition: If renewed restrictions are observed and GROCERY_PHARM > -2 and RESIDENTIAL > 10, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days is higher than its last 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Seasonal transition from summer to autumn reduces PARKS mobility as outdoor leisure becomes less attractive, shifting spending toward indoor retail venues and raising RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -16.0 at t-2w to -23.0 at t-1w then rebounded to -15.3 at t-0w
failure_condition: If PARKS declines over the next 7 days and RETAIL_REC over the same period is lower than its previous 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM remains less negative than RETAIL_REC and RESIDENTIAL stays above 9, households are still prioritizing essential errands and home time over discretionary retail, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM > -6 and RESIDENTIAL > 9 over the next 14 days but RETAIL_REC mean is higher than its last 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week rebound in PARKS of more than 5 points, interacting with a rising TRANSIT series, signals a broad outdoor mobility recovery that spills over into retail and recreation, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from -23.0 at t-1w to -15.3 at t-0w, a 7.7-point increase, while TRANSIT rose to -29.1
failure_condition: If PARKS rises more than 5 points week-on-week while TRANSIT also rises, but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days is lower than its previous 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT crossing above -30 marks a policy-enabled recovery in public transport use that reduces the cost of accessing retail districts, so RETAIL_REC rises over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT t-0w = -29.1, first crossing above -30 in the four-week window
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains above -30 for two consecutive weeks but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than its last 28-day mean.
